definitions.gloss: peerage; title of nobility; rank of nobility
definitions.explanation: A hereditary or granted rank within a system of nobility. In Japan, the peerage system (華族制度) existed from 1869 to 1947.

examples.japanese: {爵位|しゃくい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{授|さず}ける→授ける：10350_sazukeru⟧。
examples.english: To confer a title of nobility.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{功績|こうせき}→功績：04143_kouseki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧{爵位|しゃくい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{与|あた}えられた→与える：01821_ataeru⟧。
examples.english: He was granted a peerage for his achievements.

examples.japanese: ⟦{戦後|せんご}→戦後：12853_sengo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{改革|かいかく}→改革：04815_kaikaku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{爵位|しゃくい}⟦{制度|せいど}→制度：03291_seido⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{廃止|はいし}→廃止：12483_haishi⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Japan's peerage system was abolished in the postwar reforms.

notes: Japan had a five-rank peerage system modeled on European nobility: ⟦{公爵|こうしゃく}→公爵：17797_koushaku⟧ (duke/prince), {侯爵|こうしゃく} (marquis), ⟦{伯爵|はくしゃく}→伯爵：11721_hakushaku⟧ (count/earl), {子爵|ししゃく} (viscount), and ⟦{男爵|だんしゃく}→男爵：13585_danshaku⟧ (baron). This system was abolished with the 1947 constitution. The word now appears mainly in historical contexts and translations of Western literature. Common collocations: {爵位|しゃくい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{授|さず}ける→授ける：10350_sazukeru⟧ (confer a peerage), {爵位|しゃくい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{剥奪|はくだつ}→剥奪：15499_hakudatsu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (strip of a peerage).
